sn9.2:1.1: On one occasion a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain woodland thicket.
sn9.2:1.2: Now on that occasion when that bhikkhu had gone for his day’s abiding he fell asleep.
sn9.2:1.3: Then the devatā that inhabited that woodland thicket, having compassion for that bhikkhu, desiring his good, desiring to stir up a sense of urgency in him, approached him and addressed him in verses:
sn9.2:2.3: What need do you have for sleep?
sn9.2:2.4: What slumber [can there be] for one afflicted, Stricken, pierced by the dart?
sn9.2:3.2: With which you left behind the home life
sn9.2:4.2: Though the dullard is enthralled with them.
sn9.2:4.3: When he’s free, detached among those bound,
sn9.2:5.1: When, by the removal of desire and lust
sn9.2:6.1: When, by breaking ignorance with knowledge
sn9.2:6.2: And by destruction of the taints,
sn9.2:7.1: When he is energetic and resolute,
